one-line thesis: Shadowfax delivered record profitability (PAT INR 112cr FY26, +17x YoY) driven by operating leverage and mix shift to high-margin D2C/Vertical QC, while aggressively expanding asset-heavy sortation capacity and launching a 100-dark-store strategy for vertical quick commerce to capture the next wave of digital penetration.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,237cr (Q4, +74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ); FY26 Rev: INR 4,200cr (+69% YoY). EBITDA: INR 58cr (Q4, 4.7% margin vs 4.3% Q3, 0.7% YoY); FY26 Adj EBITDA: INR 159cr (~3x FY25). PAT: INR 56cr (Q4, 4.5% margin); FY26 PAT: INR 112cr vs INR 6cr FY25. Order Book: Not disclosed (flow business). Net Debt: Not explicitly stated; Capex funded via ops/cash. One-offs: Dual running costs for new sortation centers (e.g., OneNCR) and rapid real estate expansion (35% increase in space Sep-Mar) temporarily suppress margins despite record profitability.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 27-30% overall (FY27); Hyperlocal: 45-50% YoY. Margin: 100-120 bps expansion annually until FY28, then 200-250 bps/year to reach early double-digit steady-state EBITDA. Order Inflow: Targeting 17,000 pin codes by FY27 end (from 15,600). Capex: INR 180-190cr for FY27 (flat YoY absolute), with <10% allocated to dark stores; majority in sortation automation.
order book & pipeline: N/A (Transaction-based logistics flow); Key metric is volume growth and pin code coverage (15,600 currently, targeting 17,000 by FY27 end).
segment / subsidiary detail: Express Parcel (75% of rev): Gaining share from inefficient 3PLs and insourced arms; D2C/SME segment growing 2.5x YoY with 15-20% higher pricing. Hyperlocal: +50% YoY, +16% QoQ; onboarded Amazon Now; focusing on vertical QC. Other Logistics: INR 80cr (wind-down of low-value experiments complete, pivoting to critical logistics via CriticaLog).
growth verticals / optionality: 1) D2C/SME direct onboarding (Shadowfax 360) targeting 15-16 lakh sellers. 2) Large shipment capability (white goods) expanding to 10,000 pin codes. 3) Vertical Quick Commerce: Setting up 100 dark stores in FY27 for specialized categories (grocery, fashion, hardware) with 30-45 min delivery. 4) AI adoption reducing technical barriers for SMEs and optimizing routing/utilization.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin 4.7%; FY26 PAT margin 4.5%. Cost structure: ~50% partner expense (crowdsourced), ~18-19% trucking, <10% fuel (pass-through via surcharge). Margin expansion driven by mix shift to high-margin D2C/Vertical QC and operating leverage from automated sortation centers. Current drag from dual-running costs during facility transitions (6-8 months ramp).
capex / expansion: FY26 Capex: ~4.5% of revenue. FY27 Guidance: INR 180-190cr (absolute flat vs FY26). Allocation: >60% in sortation centers over last 3 years; 85% in sortation + last mile hubs. Dark stores <10% of FY27 capex. Strategy: Asset-heavy under roof (automation), asset-light on road.
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic capacity expansion (sortation automation, dark stores) and geographic penetration (120-150 new pin codes/month). Acquired 100% of CriticaLog (high-value logistics) for integration. No dividend/buyback mentioned; reinvestment mode for 10x scale.
risks & watch-items: 1) Geopolitical volatility impacting crude/fuel prices (mitigated by surcharge). 2) Execution risk in scaling 100 dark stores and integrating vertical QC clients. 3) Intense competition in quick commerce leading to pricing pressure (though mgmt cites fragmented client base reduces single-client leverage). 4) Ramp-up period costs for new facilities impacting short-term margins.
management quality / tone: Highly confident and aggressive; emphasizing 'phenomenal tailwinds,' 'record profitability,' and 'audacious bets' on vertical QC and AI. Tone suggests inflection point where early capex investments are beginning to yield operating leverage.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) Shift from horizontal to vertical quick commerce as the primary growth lever, with Shadowfax positioning as the natural 3PL for capital-constrained vertical players. 2) AI is not just an efficiency tool but a demand generator by lowering technical barriers for SMEs to go online. 3) Network design philosophy: Fewer, larger last-mile nodes to optimize transportation mesh, contrary to industry trend of hyper-fragmented nodes. 4) Dual-running costs for 6-8 months per new facility create a temporary margin drag that masks true steady-state profitability.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rapid shift of SME/D2C sellers to online channels requiring reliable, high-margin logistics partners. | Shadowfax Technologies | beneficiary | High | Direct access to 15-16 lakh SMEs via Shadowfax 360 offers 15-20% higher realization than enterprise contracts; first-mover advantage in vertical QC dark stores. |
| Horizontal quick commerce players facing margin pressure and needing flexible, asset-light fulfillment partners. | Quick Commerce Platforms (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | Shadowfax's onboarding of Amazon Now and focus on vertical QC provides scalable infrastructure without capex burden for platforms. |
| Inefficient traditional 3PLs losing market share to consolidated, tech-enabled players. | Traditional/Fragmented 3PLs | loser | High | Shadowfax gaining 28-29% 3PL market share (up from 17-18% YoY) primarily at the expense of inefficient players and insourced arms. |

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

hero.oneLiner: New-age, technology-led 3PL company leveraging technology to facilitate digital commerce, with a service network covering 14,758 Indian pin codes and India's largest crowdsourced last-mile delivery fleet among 3PL e-commerce players.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: New-age, technology-led 3PL company leveraging technology to facilitate digital commerce, with a service network covering 14,758 Indian pin codes and India's largest crowdsourced last-mile delivery fleet among 3PL e-commerce players.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Provides express logistics (forward parcel delivery, reverse pickup, hand-in-hand exchange, prime same-day/next-day delivery), hyperlocal delivery (quick commerce, on-demand) and other logistics services including critical logistics to enterprise clients such as Meesho, Flipkart, Myntra, Swiggy, Bigbasket, Zepto, Nykaa, Blinkit, Zomato, Uber, Licious and ONDC. Operates an asset-light, fully leased nationwide network of 4,299 touchpoints and 53 sort centers (over 3.50 million sq ft of operational space) reaching 14,758 pin codes, with a gig-based last-mile fleet (205,864 Average Quarterly Unique Transacting Delivery Partners in H1 FY26) and a dedicated linehaul fleet of more than 3,000 trucks daily. Platform processed 436.36 million orders in FY25 (29.77% CAGR from FY23) and 294.45 million orders in H1 FY26.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Criticalog India Private Limited — Subsidiary (89.59% of total shareholding acquired via SPA/SHA dated November 22, 2024): Bengaluru-based logistics provider engaged in freight management, air and road express delivery, freight forwarding, intermodal transportation, warehousing, customs house clearance, trade compliance and supply chain management
- Flipkart Internet Private Limited — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 4,000.00 million; Flipkart is also named among major e-commerce clients
- Eight Roads Investments Mauritius II Limited (formerly FIL Capital Investments (Mauritius) II Limited) — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 1,970.00 million
- International Finance Corporation — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 655.49 million
- Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd. — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 654.20 million
- Nokia Growth Partners IV, L.P. — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 593.00 million
- NewQuest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 450.00 million
- Mirae Asset - Naver New Growth Fund I — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 375.00 million
- Mirae Asset - GS Retail New Growth Fund I — Investor Selling Shareholder: OFS up to Rs 375.00 million

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Express:** Forward express parcel delivery (incl. open-box, scheduled time-slot, cash-on-delivery), Reverse pickup logistics (largest 3PL for reverse pick-up shipments by order volume, FY25 and H1 FY26), Hand-in-hand exchange (incl. doorstep quality checks), Prime delivery - same-day and next-day delivery (operational in more than 30 cities; largest 3PL for same-day delivery by order volume)
- **Hyperlocal:** Quick commerce deliveries (market leader in 3PL Q-Commerce solutions by order volume, FY25 and H1 FY26), On-demand hyperlocal deliveries
- **Other services:** Mobility, Critical logistics, Freight management, air and road express delivery, freight forwarding, intermodal transportation, warehousing, customs house clearance, trade compliance and supply chain management (via subsidiary Criticalog India Private Limited)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Horizontal and non-horizontal e-commerce (e-commerce shipment market share ~8% in FY22 to ~23% in H1 FY26)
- Quick commerce
- Food marketplace
- On-demand mobility
- Majority of revenue from operations derived from services delivering directly to the end-customer

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Asset-light, fully leased model across logistics facilities and linehaul while retaining ownership of automation and machinery for operational control. Integrated network spans first-mile pick-up and return-to-origin centers, middle-mile sorting, last-mile delivery and linehaul (more than 3,000 leased trucks daily, all leased from third-party fleet partners), interconnected via a hybrid mesh-based linehaul network with dynamic routing. Last mile is executed through a crowdsourced gig-based delivery partner fleet (205,864 Average Quarterly Unique Transacting Delivery Partners for six months ended September 30, 2025, across more than 2,300 cities) plus franchisee partners on a variable cost model; India's largest crowdsourced last-mile delivery fleet among 3PL e-commerce players (RedSeer). Partnerships with OEMs provide delivery partners access to EVs on a rental basis via a three-way EV marketplace (delivery partners, OEMs, quick-commerce clients); airline partnerships enable next-day delivery in metropolitan cities. Proprietary in-house technology stack (supply-demand allocation engine, Frodo delivery-partner lifecycle system with UIDAI/NSDL touchless onboarding, SF Shield fraud detection with track-and-trace, SF Maps address intelligence, APIs for client integration) orchestrates the network. Forward extension into multi-brand dark store operations and strategic insourcing of unbundled supply-chain services; acquisition of 89.59% of Criticalog India Private Limited (November 22, 2024) added freight management, air and road express, freight forwarding, intermodal transportation, warehousing, customs house clearance, trade compliance and supply chain management capabilities.

customers.title: Oem (RHP)
customers.body: Certain OEMs (unnamed) partnered to provide the last-mile delivery fleet access to EVs on a rental basis; two-wheeler EV rental marketplace established for delivery partners

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Variable, gig-based delivery partner cost structure keeps delivery costs proportional to volumes, lowering fixed costs versus an employed fleet
- Asset-light model: fully leased logistics facilities and linehaul with ownership only of automation and machinery; franchisee partners on variable cost model enable geographic expansion with minimal fixed overheads
- Hybrid mesh-based linehaul network with dynamic routing algorithm enables node-to-node connectivity, optimized cost structures and operating leverage
- Margins are not tracked at service-line level and likely differ across service lines, geographies, weight profiles, clients and lanes - changes in business mix can move contribution margin, EBITDA and PAT
- Adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 1.96% (FY25) to 2.86% (H1 FY26) on revenue growth (order volume CAGR 29.77% FY23-FY25; 50.11% H1-on-H1)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to expand the portfolio of clients and services
- Strengthen and expand the network
- Continue to invest in technology
- Strategically expand vehicle leasing for cost-effective logistics operations
- Expand the business internationally
- Pursue strategic investment opportunities (e.g. Criticalog acquisition)
- Enhance client experience through the three levers of Velocity (optimize click-to-doorstep time), Versatility (tailored solutions on one platform) and Value (low delivery costs)
- Promote EV and bicycle adoption on the platform and integrate sustainable logistics practices (two-wheeler EV rental marketplace for delivery partners)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: No manufacturing capex; growth is network- and acquisition-led. The company plans to keep expanding its fully leased, asset-light logistics network (4,299 touchpoints across 14,758 pin codes as of September 30, 2025) and hybrid mesh-based linehaul (3,000+ dedicated trucks daily), strategically expand vehicle leasing, expand internationally, and pursue strategic investments - it acquired 89.59% of Criticalog India Private Limited (agreement dated November 22, 2024) to add critical logistics, freight management and supply-chain services. The Offer comprises a Fresh Issue of up to Rs 10,000.00 million plus an Offer for Sale aggregating Rs 9,072.69 million; the company will not receive OFS proceeds.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Agile and customisable logistics services that enable faster go-to-market for clients
- Largest last-mile gig-based delivery partner infrastructure - India's largest crowdsourced last-mile delivery fleet among 3PL e-commerce players by average monthly transacting delivery partners (FY25 and H1 FY26)
- Extensive nationwide network - 4,299 touchpoints, 14,758 pin codes, gig partners in more than 2,300 cities and towns
- Proprietary and agile technology capabilities - multi-category supply-demand allocation engine, client APIs, SF Maps AI-based mapping infrastructure, delivery-partner app, all built in-house
- Proven business model with focus on profitability while delivering healthy growth
- Experienced management team supported by entrepreneurial founders
- Fastest growing 3PL company of scale in India as of March 31, 2025; e-commerce shipment market share expanded from ~8% (FY22) to ~23% (H1 FY26)
- Market leader in reverse pickup shipments, 3PL quick-commerce solutions and same-day delivery by order volume (FY25 and H1 FY26)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- History of net losses and negative cash flows — Losses of Rs 1,426.38 million (FY23) and Rs 118.82 million (FY24), with negative operating/investing/financing cash flows in certain periods; management expects operating expenses to increase and losses/negative cash flows may recur
- Thin, opaque margins with business-mix sensitivity — Company does not track margins at service-line level; contribution margin, EBITDA and PAT likely differ across service lines, geographies, weight profiles, clients and lanes, so any mix shift can swing profitability (Adjusted EBITDA margin was only 1.96% in FY25)
- Dependence on gig-based crowdsourced delivery partner network — Last-mile execution relies on 200,000+ gig delivery partners and franchisees rather than an employed fleet; the variable-cost model is core to the value proposition
- Client concentration in large digital commerce platforms — Revenue depends on enterprise e-commerce, quick commerce, food and mobility platforms (Meesho, Flipkart, Swiggy, Zepto, Blinkit, Zomato, Uber etc.); majority of revenue comes from direct end-customer delivery services for these clients
- Intensifying competition in quick commerce logistics — The quick commerce sector expects more entrants, intensifying competition; providers must continuously innovate and optimize processes to sustain profitability and market position
- Acquisition/expansion execution risk — Growth initiatives including the 89.59% Criticalog acquisition, international expansion and vehicle-leasing expansion may cost more than expected or may not result in increased revenue

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Continue to expand the portfolio of clients and services as part of growing the value-velocity-versatility proposition.**
- **Strengthen and expand the logistics network and continue to invest in technology.**
- **Strategically expand vehicle leasing for cost-effective logistics operations.**
- **Expand the business internationally beyond India.**
- **Pursue strategic investment opportunities; the acquisition of 89.59% of Criticalog India Private Limited (agreement dated November 22, 2024) adds freight management, air/road express, freight forwarding, warehousing, customs clearance and …**
- **Management expects operating expenses to increase as growth initiatives are pursued, and the company may continue to experience losses and negative cash flows in the future.**
- **Promote EV and bicycle usage on the platform (two-wheeler EV rental marketplace, OEM partnerships); in H1 FY26 an average of 23.62% of hyperlocal delivery orders per month were completed using EVs or bicycles (baseline to track).**
- **Raise a Fresh Issue of Equity Shares aggregating up to Rs 10,000.00 million (alongside an Offer for Sale of Rs 9,072.69 million from which the company receives no proceeds).**
